newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil slips with crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil slips with crude.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps slipped at midday on Monday in quiet trading but the market remains well supported by the sustained buying from a group of traders, brokers said.
"The market came off slightly this morning because of crude but sentiment is unchanged," one broker said.
May gas oil swaps were last quoted at $25.60/$25.75 per barrel, down from Friday's $25.80/$25.90, brokers said. May traded earlier in the day at $25.70, they said.
June swaps were quoted at $24.60/$24.75, also down from Friday's $24.80/$24.90, brokers said. The May/June spread was seen at $1.00/$1.10 per barrel, they said.
June Brent crude closed down 15 cents to 18.27 per barrel on Friday in London.

The wide May/June spread is expected to deter further arbitrage exports from the West as the East/West spread - valued through the May gas oil on the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) - is at $18.15 per tonne.
This compares to the earlier spread of about $30 per tonne which was the basis for the past arbitrage exports during March and April of over 15 million barrels to Asia.
May gas oil closed up 75 cents to $165.50 per tonne on the IPE on Friday.
Traders said apart from the tight freight market, the low East-West spread will not lead to new exports.
On Friday, the traders who have been responsible for the purchase of over 15 million barrels on the Singapore market since March 3 bought two more cargoes.

The two 150,000-barrel cargoes traded at $26.70 and $26.30 per barrel for May loading on a free-on-board basis, suggesting that the traders are not expected to pull out of the sot market at least until end April.
The fuel oil swaps also edged down slightly with the weaker crude with May last quoted at $97.25/$98.50 per tonne from Friday's $97.75/$98.25, brokers said.
